entities.summary: Bernardino Ochino (1487–1564) was a prominent Italian Protestant reformer who played a pivotal role in the Protestant Reformation in Europe. Born in Italy, Ochino was raised a Roman Catholic but later converted to Protestantism, becoming a key figure in the spread of the Reformation. His influence extended to various regions, including Switzerland and Germany, where he worked closely with other reformers such as Huldrych Zwingli. Ochino's religious beliefs were shaped by his exposure to Protestant ideas during his travels and his interactions with influential thinkers of the time. He also played a significant role in the development of the concept of 'sola scriptura,' which emphasized the authority of the Bible alone. Ochino's legacy can be seen in the continued influence of Protestantism in Europe and beyond, with his ideas contributing to the shaping of modern Western Christianity. Despite his significant contributions, Ochino's life and work remain somewhat overshadowed by other prominent figures of the Protestant Reformation. This oversight is partly due to the limited availability of primary sources about Ochino's life and teachings, which have made it difficult for historians to reconstruct his biography with precision. Nevertheless, Ochino's impact on the development of Protestantism and his contributions to the Reformation make him an important figure in the history of Western Christianity.
